This is suboptimal because the order in which vertices are colored significantly affects the final number of colors used. A well-known improvement is to use the DSATUR (Degree of Saturation) algorithm, which dynamically selects the next vertex to color based on the number of distinct colors already used by its neighbors. This heuristic tends to produce much better colorings than static orderings. DSATUR prioritizes vertices that are most constrained (have the highest saturation degree), breaking ties by choosing vertices with the highest degree in the uncolored subgraph.
